result.topic_en: Euler states and begins solving Problem III: finding the space curve that maximizes or minimizes the integral of X·ds, where X is a function of x alone. He shows that the curve lies in a plane and derives the differential equations of its projections.
result.transcription:
28
Problema III.
Invenire lineam curvam ternis coordinatis x, y et z contentam, in qua haec formula integralis: $\int X\sqrt{\partial x^2+\partial y^2+\partial z^2}$
maximum minimumve adipiscatur valorem, existente
X functione quacunque ipsius x.
Solutio.
19. Hic ergo, ob $\partial y = p\,\partial x$ et $\partial z = q\,\partial x$, erit
$V = X\sqrt{1+pp+qq}$, ubi brevitatis gratia ponamus
$\sqrt{1+pp+qq}=s$, ita ut sit $V=Xs$. Quia igitur ipsae litterae
$y$ et $z$ non insunt, erit tam $N=0$ quam $N'=0$; deinde
ob $\partial s=\frac{p\partial p+q\partial q}{s}$, erit $P=\frac{Xp}{s}$ et $P'=\frac{Xq}{s}$, unde binae aequationes solutionem continentes erunt $\partial P=0$ et $\partial P'=0$,
sicque habebimus $\frac{Xp}{s}=a$ et $\frac{Xq}{s}=b=na$.
20. Hinc igitur statim patet fore $\frac{q}{p}=n$, sive $q=np$,
hincque porro $\partial z=n\partial y$, et integrando $z=ny+c$, ita ut
projectio in planum BOC facta sit linea recta, ideoque
tota curva quaesita in certo plano existat. Deinde vero
cum sit $s=\sqrt{1+(nn+1)pp}$, erit $Xp=a\sqrt{1+(nn+1)pp}$;
unde, posito brevitatis gratia $nn+1=m$, colligimus
$p=\frac{a}{\sqrt{(X^2-aamm)}}$. Sicque pro utraque projectione quaesita habebimus has aequationes differentiales:
$\partial y=\frac{a\partial x}{\sqrt{(X^2-mmaa)}}$ et $\partial z=\frac{na\partial x}{\sqrt{(X^2-mmaa)}}$.
